section: Methods of measuring national income - product, income and expenditure methods; difficulties
subsections: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method
Method to sectors - how India applies each

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the value added method of measuring national income?
o: It sums the value added by every producing unit
It sums transfer payments received by households
It sums only government expenditure on final goods
It sums factor payments made to all households
accepted.x: The production or product method measures national income by summing the value added by each producing unit, which is equal to the value of the final product after avoiding double counting.
accepted.tq: Use the exact definition of the method rather than its alternative names.
accepted.sec: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Income Method of measuring national income is also known as the
accepted.x: The income method is also called the factor income or factor payment method because it aggregates incomes earned by factors of production.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the alternative names of the three methods.
accepted.sec: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Under the Income Method, which of the following is included in the computation of national income?
1. Compensation of employees
2. Operating surplus consisting of rent, interest and profit
3. Mixed income
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The income method includes compensation of employees, operating surplus such as rent, interest and profit, and mixed income.
accepted.tq: Test whether all listed components belong to the same accounting method.
accepted.sec: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the expenditure method, national income is measured by aggregating
accepted.x: The expenditure method adds consumption, investment, government expenditure and net exports, represented by C + I + G + (X − M).
accepted.tq: Recall the expenditure identity and check the direction of net exports.
accepted.sec: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Cost and accounting method — Final expenditure method
accepted.x: Cost and accounting method is not a recognised method of measuring national income. The expenditure method is also called the consumption-and-investment or final expenditure method.
accepted.tq: Find the non-method among closely related official terms.
accepted.sec: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Economic Survey formula for GDP under the Income Method:
1. Compensation of employees is included.
2. Consumption of fixed capital is included.
3. Production taxes net of production subsidies are included.
4. Gross operating surplus is included.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Economic Survey formula is compensation of employees + consumption of fixed capital + production taxes minus production subsidies + gross operating surplus.
accepted.tq: Check each term in a multi-part accounting formula.
accepted.sec: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which component of expenditure has traditionally constituted the largest share of India's GDP, at about 59 per cent?
accepted.x: Private consumption expenditure is the largest expenditure component, accounting for about 59 per cent of GDP.
accepted.tq: Use the largest-share comparison in the expenditure composition.
accepted.sec: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the relative behaviour of the major expenditure components in India?
o: Business investment is the most volatile component
Government spending is more volatile than business investment
Net exports are the largest and least volatile component
Private consumption is the smallest component
accepted.x: Business investment is the most volatile component of expenditure, while private consumption is the largest and net exports form the last component in the stated ordering.
accepted.tq: Compare size and volatility rather than treating all expenditure components alike.
accepted.sec: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): India's relatively high share of private consumption makes its economy less exposed to global swings.
Reason (R): Private consumption accounts for about 59 per cent of GDP and is the largest expenditure component.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the large share of private consumption explains why the economy is comparatively less exposed to fluctuations in global demand and trade.
accepted.tq: Test whether the quantitative reason directly explains the economic conclusion.
accepted.sec: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the stated current data, Gross Fixed Capital Formation as a percentage of nominal GDP in the first quarter of 2026–27 was
accepted.x: Nominal Gross Fixed Capital Formation rose to 34.3 per cent of GDP in the first quarter of 2026–27, from 31.4 per cent.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the current value from the preceding comparison value.
accepted.sec: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the current growth figures stated for the first quarter of 2026–27?
o: Real GFCF grew by 7.1 per cent and private consumption by 11.9 per cent
Real GFCF grew by 34.3 per cent and private consumption by 31.4 per cent
Real GFCF grew by 31.4 per cent and private consumption by 34.3 per cent
Real GFCF grew by 11.9 per cent and private consumption by 7.1 per cent
accepted.x: Real GFCF grew by 11.9 per cent, while private consumption grew by 7.1 per cent in the stated period.
accepted.tq: Keep nominal shares, real growth rates and comparison figures separate.
accepted.sec: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is included in national income despite involving no actual rent payment by the owner?
o: Rent-free government housing provided as a transfer
A gift received by a household
accepted.x: Imputed rent of owner-occupied houses is included because the housing service has an economic value even when no rent is actually paid.
accepted.tq: Identify imputed economic services among transfer and financial items.
accepted.sec: Inclusion/exclusion test  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is treated as a factor payment and is therefore included in national income?
o: Interest earned on a productive loan
Pension received by a retired employee
accepted.x: Interest on productive loans is a return to a factor of production and is included. Pensions, scholarships and gifts are transfer payments.
accepted.tq: Separate factor payments from receipts that involve no service in return.
accepted.sec: Inclusion/exclusion test  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A second-hand car is sold through a dealer. Which part of this transaction is included in national income?
o: The original purchase price and the resale price together
The entire sale value of the car
Only the broker's or dealer's commission
Neither the sale value nor the commission
accepted.x: The second-hand good itself was counted when originally produced. In the resale, only the current service represented by the broker's or dealer's commission is included.
accepted.tq: Apply the current-production test to resale transactions.
accepted.sec: Inclusion/exclusion test  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following transactions is excluded from national income as a purely financial transaction?
accepted.x: Transactions in shares and bonds merely transfer ownership of financial assets and do not represent current production. Production for self-use and changes in inventories are included.
accepted.tq: Distinguish financial asset transfers from current production.
accepted.sec: Inclusion/exclusion test  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is included in national income as production for self-use?
o: Farm output consumed by the producing household
A gift received by a farmer
accepted.x: Self-consumed farm output is included because it represents production of goods. Unpaid household services and public-debt interest are excluded under the stated rules.
accepted.tq: Test whether self-use involves measurable production of a good.
accepted.sec: Inclusion/exclusion test  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Item — Treatment in national income
1. Change in inventories — Included
2. Tax revenue as such — Excluded
3. Interest on public debt — Included
4. Housewives' unpaid services — Excluded
accepted.x: Changes in inventories are included, while tax revenue as such, interest on public debt and unpaid services of housewives are excluded. Therefore, statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct.
accepted.tq: Classify each item by asking whether it is factor income or current production.
accepted.sec: Inclusion/exclusion test  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In India's national income estimation, the production or value-added method is principally applied to
o: Public administration and real estate only
accepted.x: The production method is principally used for agriculture and allied activities, mining and manufacturing.
accepted.tq: Map each method to the sectors for which it is principally used.
accepted.sec: Method to sectors - how India applies each  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Income Method is principally used in India for estimating income generated by which group of activities?
o: Trade, transport, banking, real estate and public administration
accepted.x: The income method is used for service activities such as trade, transport, banking, real estate, public administration and other services.
accepted.tq: Use sectoral grouping to distinguish the production and income methods.
accepted.sec: Method to sectors - how India applies each  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the application of the expenditure method in India:
1. It is used in part for construction.
2. Expenditure data such as PFCE serves as a check on estimates.
3. It is used as a cross-check of demand-side components.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The expenditure method is used partly for construction, and expenditure data including PFCE acts as a check on and cross-check of demand-side estimates.
accepted.tq: Combine the stated use, data source and checking function of one method.
accepted.sec: Method to sectors - how India applies each  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 2022–23 national accounts series uses HCES 2022–23 to benchmark
accepted.x: The 2022–23 series benchmarks private final consumption expenditure using HCES 2022–23.
accepted.tq: Match the survey acronym and year with the expenditure component it benchmarks.
accepted.sec: Method to sectors - how India applies each  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What is the principal purpose of aligning Supply and Use Tables with national accounts in the 2022–23 series?
o: To replace the income method with the expenditure method
To reduce discrepancies between production-side and expenditure-side GDP
To eliminate all transfer payments from GDP
accepted.x: The alignment of Supply and Use Tables with national accounts is intended to reduce discrepancies between production-side and expenditure-side GDP estimates.
accepted.tq: Identify the purpose of an accounting reconciliation measure rather than its coverage.
accepted.sec: Method to sectors - how India applies each  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India's sectoral application of national-income methods?
o: Expenditure method for all sectors; production method only as a cross-check
Production method for agriculture and manufacturing; income method for services; expenditure method partly for construction
Income method for agriculture and mining; production method for services; expenditure method only for banking
Production method for services; income method only for construction; no expenditure check
accepted.x: India applies the production method to agriculture, mining and manufacturing, the income method to services, and the expenditure method partly to construction and as a cross-check.
accepted.tq: Compare the complete sector-method mapping before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: Method to sectors - how India applies each  [APPSC]
